version.changelog: v1.6.0 (2026-10-20) - Clean reworked: zone-shaped knob authority (internal SOFT 0-50% / MID 50-83% / HARD 83-100% zones), gated by AIR (Clean only polices the boost once AIR passes ~half, soft knee in), with mode ceilings: INST may eat the whole boost on harsh peaks; BUS caps the reduction at 3 dB so a mix bus or master can never be torn apart. Clean still only reduces the AIR boost, never the source itself. - De-harsh detector thresholds lowered for sensitivity: BUS -24 dBFS, INST -32 dBFS (were -18 / -26). - DE-HARSH LED: new eager law. It lights early and climbs fast with detector activity and knob position - a livelier visual than the gentle real reduction behind it. - New vu_off.png (companion graphics): the needle now rests parked at the left stop when powered off instead of disappearing. - Mouse wheel: every knob and lever (incl. MODE, OPERATION and POWER) answers to the scroll wheel, one step per notch; levers are directional - scroll up/down drives them to their ends and holds them there. Only the IN/GR/OUT meter selector stays click-only. v1.5.9 (2026-10-17) - Fixed VU level followers (IN and OUT): the old one-pole follower chased the instantaneous rectified signal instead of holding the peak, so on a steady sine it settled ~0.6 dB below the true peak at every level (measured: 0 -> -0.6, -6 -> -6.6, -12 -> -12.6 dB). The followers now hold the peak and decay multiplicatively (150 ms release), the same form as the peak meters: residual sine ripple <= 0.07 dB. Needle smoothing and the scale mapping are unchanged. v1.5.8 (2026-10-10) - New OPERATION switch (BUS/INST) with horizontal 2-pos lever, placed symmetrically opposite the DE-HARSH LED: BUS mode (left): 160 Hz sub crossover, -18 dBFS de-harsh threshold, standard drive voicing — for mix bus and mastering. INST mode (right): 90 Hz sub crossover, -26 dBFS de-harsh threshold (creative tool, LED responds on normal material), warmer drive voicing (stronger even-harmonic emphasis) — for individual instruments and tracks. v1.5.7 (2026-10-10) - Fixed sub crossover: the highpass section used 3 biquads (6th-order) instead of 2 (4th-order), breaking the Linkwitz-Riley reconstruction and causing a ~5 dB dip at ~154 Hz whenever the sub section was engaged. Now true LR4 4th-order on both bands. v1.5.6 (2026-10-09) - VU face graphics corrected: scale graduation now matches the needle programming exactly. v1.5.5 (2026-10-09) - VU meter ballistics: dedicated level follower with 5ms attack and 150ms release (Tukan-style), plus asymmetric needle smoothing (fast attack 0.75, smooth release 0.35) for analog feel. v1.5.4 (2026-10-09) - Reduced hit area on the 4 levers (SUB BYPASS, SAFETY LIMITER, AIR BYPASS, DRIVE POWER) and on the MODE selector: now ±48px horizontal and 565-614 vertical, fitted to the graphic edge. POWER unchanged. v1.5.3 (2026-10-09) - Code cleanup: removed obsolete comments (references to previous design sizes and "preview build"). v1.5.2 (2026-10-09) - Fixed @gfx block order: the size declaration (@gfx 1024 700) is now the first instruction in the section, so REAPER opens the window at the correct size. v1.5.1 (2026-10-09) - VU Meter Mode now defaults to IN (was GR). v1.5 (2026-10-09) - Display name simplificado a "FMA Sub-Air" (sin número de versión) para evitar conflictos en futuras actualizaciones. La versión se sigue controlando vía @version para ReaPack. v1.4 (2026-10-04) - NEW: Vintage Drive saturator — warm tube-style even-harmonic saturation ("silk" voicing: asymmetric triode-like curve, ultra-soft knee, subtlety-first). Red DRIVE knob (0% = transparent) plus FOCUS selector (Sub / Full / Air) so the user chooses which band gets saturated. 2x oversampled saturation path for alias-free harmonics. Drive power switch (ON = processing). v1.3 (2026-10-01) - GUI controls now update the DSP in real time (no need to press play) - Per-section bypass switches respond instantly v1.2 - Initial FMA Series release

version.author: Justin Johnson (original ReEQ); FMA Edition by Free Mix Audio
version.changelog: v1.2.5 (2026-10-29) - Improvements: the theme selector moved into Settings > GUI; footer pills size to their text and wrap to a second row when they do not fit. - The footer and the node panel never vanish for lack of space: the footer wraps to 2-3 rows at any size and the graph yields; when the panel does not fit it rolls up into a tab (node, frequency, gain) and everything stays reachable. - Staged panel collapse: as the window narrows the panel hides controls from the outside in, and the hidden ones stay fully editable in the "..." overflow panel, paged with arrows. - Note: the lack of space only shows up when the window ends up logically small, in practice for users running Windows display scaling (e.g. 175%); at 100% with a normal window size the layout is unchanged. - Fixes (both pre-existing in the released build): pressing Settings no longer deselects the node; slow-click re-select no longer jumps the gain (~-4 dB). - The plugin code is the 1.2.0-fma.27 build; audio, slider map, themes, SILK and limiter unchanged since fma.20 (ECO bit-identical; HQ shows only the pre-existing startup jitter). v1.2.4 (2026-10-25) - Node menu off-by-one fix (bug reported in Windows: pressing High Shelf in the node's right-click menu activated Low Shelf). When the "Dynamic" row was added to that menu its separator was forgotten, so "Zero Gain" and "Dynamic" fused into one row and every later item shifted one position down. One line restores the separator; the menu is again Disable / Invert Gain / Zero Gain / Dynamic / Shape / Slope / Stereo Placement / Split / Duplicate / Delete with the original numbering. - Panel dial hit areas made exact (bug reported in Windows: dials reacted in empty space and over neighbouring dials). The dial grab test was a square of half-side r + gfx_texth*2 around each centre - at the panel's 64 px dial spacing it overlapped every neighbour by 24-34 px, stole 6 px of the DYN pill, and reached empty space above each knob. The test is now the drawn knob circle only (radius r + 3 + 3*retina), so no two activation areas touch in any direction. The value text under each dial no longer grabs it. - The plugin code is the 1.2.0-fma.22 build; audio, slider map, themes, SILK and limiter unchanged since fma.20. v1.2.3 (2026-10-23) - Repository metadata: the package description now points original-ReEQ users to the drop-in twin (ReEQ.jsfx, manual install) available in this repository's Releases. The plugin itself is UNCHANGED - this is the 1.2.0-fma.20 build. v1.2.2 (2026-10-22) - Repository metadata fix: the two include files are now declared as ONE @provides block (the indexer's parser keeps only the last repeated @provides tag, so 1.2.0/1.2.1 installed without the spectrum include). The plugin itself is UNCHANGED - this is the 1.2.0-fma.20 build. v1.2.1 (2026-10-22) - Repository metadata release: the changelog is now published in full (house format, below) and both include files are installed together with the plugin. The plugin itself is UNCHANGED - this is the 1.2.0-fma.20 build. v1.2.0-fma.20 (2026-10-22) - Bottom row centred as ONE group on the window width, recomputed every frame: ECO/HQ, M/S, Scale, Gain, the Mid/Side gains and phase toggles, LIMIT, PANEL, AGC and SILK. The classic button widths are kept and only the gaps are computed, so the full row is visible from the moment the plugin opens - the SILK button no longer starts half-hidden at the right edge. - The theme selector moved from the top-right corner into the bottom row, as its last pill after SILK; its list opens upward, draws on top of the node panel, and while it is open the panel ignores the mouse. Settings stays alone in the corner. - Base theme renamed "FMA Solid" (slider enum, list and pill label); values, order and palettes untouched. Audio bit-identical to fma.19. v1.2.0-fma.19 (2026-10-22) - NEW: SILK (hidden slider60, HQ ONLY) - a spectral exciter stage inside the x2 oversampled path, after the SVF cascade and before decimation. Four bands split by subtraction (250 Hz / 3.5 kHz / 9 kHz) pass through asymmetric tanh shapers with unity small-signal gain, so steady tones keep ~0 dB of net EQ and only harmonics are added: lows DEEP (strong 2nd harmonic), mids DEFINED (almost no drive), highs EXPENSIVE (more drive the higher they sit). Worst alias spur measured at -100 dBFS; with SILK at 0 the stage is skipped whole and HQ renders bit-identical to fma.18. In ECO the button is drawn locked and does nothing, by design. - The limiter is finished: the factory hard clamp at 0 dBFS is replaced by a soft ceiling at -1 dBFS - bit-exact passthrough below the -3 dBFS knee, a tanh curve above it that approaches the ceiling and can never exceed it. No added latency (PDC 0 / 31 unchanged); works in both modes. - Audit fix B1: the slope dial's fade read a misspelled node variable that does not exist; it now reads the selected node like everything else. v1.2.0-fma.18 (2026-10-22) - Stage 3: six full FMA themes - Fire Storm, Ice Storm, Sand Storm, Star Rain, Sea Mist, Bronze Wall - plus the FMA base theme and Classic, selected from the GUI pill. Each theme re-palettes the WHOLE window on the fma.17 skin: tinted graphite ground and plate, buttons in the theme accent, and the spectrum drawn with a deep body, a luminous main-colour edge and near-white peaks. - Theme state lives in the new hidden slider59 "GuiTheme", appended at the END of the slider list (nothing renumbered). The selector list is drawn inside the plugin and its clicks are guarded, so they never create, delete or drag bands. Audio bit-identical to fma.17. v1.2.0-fma.17 (2026-10-21) - FMA skin buttons now wear an intense orange fill (#F26B1A) with a lighter hover and dark text - the resting buttons no longer get lost against the graph plate. Covered: the whole bottom row, Settings, the GUI tab and the node panel's own buttons. State colours unchanged: HQ keeps the house amber, "on" toggles their green, DELETE its red. - The node panel's corners are delicately rounded (radius 10) in the FMA skin only; the original translucency is untouched. Classic unchanged. Audio bit-identical to fma.16. v1.2.0-fma.16 (2026-10-21) - FMA skin buttons redrawn with EXACTLY the original capsule construction - only the colour values change. The extra outline stroke that left two little circles at the caps of every button is removed everywhere. The Classic drawing path is untouched. Audio bit-identical to fma.15. v1.2.0-fma.15 (2026-10-21) - NEW: the FMA house skin - graphite background, the graph on a recessed dark plate, flat pills, the HQ button and the selected node's ring in house amber - with a corner tab ("GUI: FMA" / "GUI: Classic") that switches skins instantly. The node panel keeps its ORIGINAL translucent background, by express design decision (a solid fill takes away what makes the original design lovely). - Skin state in the new hidden slider58 "GuiSkin", appended at the END of the slider list (nothing renumbered); a fresh instance opens in the FMA skin. Geometry, band colours, the white curve and the RTA are untouched. Audio bit-identical to fma.14. v1.2.0-fma.14 (2026-10-21) - Display-only correction: in HQ the drawn curve no longer multiplies the filter response by the half-band chain magnitude, so the graph stops reporting the oversampling chain's terminal droop and ripple toward the top octave. It now draws the filters' own response, flat to the last pixel, like the original and the reference plugins. The droop remains in the AUDIO exactly as in fma.13; it is simply not drawn. Audio bit-identical to fma.13. v1.2.0-fma.13 (2026-10-21) - HQ rebuilt with a different method: THIS EQ CARRIES NO LINEAR PHASE. HQ is now x2 minimum-phase oversampling with a self-contained half-band FIR generated by Kaiser formula at init (125 taps, stopband -109 dB, folded image residue -151 dB), working at every sample rate. Latency drops from 2559 to 31 samples, and the dynamics' timing now matches ECO. ECO bit-identical to fma.12. v1.2.0-fma.12 (2026-10-19) - Four corrections from review: the convolution kernel of the time is built paced by samples so it no longer stalls the audio thread (the design curve is drawn while it builds); the graph's left edge extends down to 10 Hz; dynamics processing is coalesced per band. v1.2.0-fma.11 (2026-10-19) - Reformulation: two quality modes only, {Eco, HQ} - the x8 stage is removed after CPU reports (a single instance could pin a real-time thread). A fresh instance always starts in ECO. v1.2.0-fma.10 (2026-10-18) - Pruning of leftover machinery from retired stages, and a fast dry-seeded start for the convolution engine of the time. v1.2.0-fma.9 (2026-10-18) - The Linear Phase engine is rebuilt on partitioned FFT convolution - the earlier direct kernel cost too much CPU to be practical. (Engine retired in fma.13.) v1.2.0-fma.8 (2026-10-17) - HQ x8 oversampling stage added. (Removed in fma.11 for CPU cost.) v1.2.0-fma.7 (2026-10-17) - The HQ half-band filter becomes self-contained: it is generated by formula at init instead of shipping fixed coefficients that only existed for 44.1 and 48 kHz - HQ now works at every sample rate (audit B7/B8). v1.2.0-fma.6 (2026-10-17) - Linear Phase kernel enlarged to 4095 taps for a steeper, cleaner response. (Engine retired in fma.13.) v1.2.0-fma.5 (2026-10-17) - The dynamics action curve is drawn at the node itself, so what the per-band dynamics is doing is visible exactly where it happens. v1.2.0-fma.4 (2026-10-16) - Dynamics display at the node completed, plus node panel fixes. v1.2.0-fma.3 (2026-10-16) - Per-band dynamics gains its own ON/OFF switch per band, and real Attack/Release times replace the fixed smoothing. v1.2.0-fma.2 (2026-10-16) - The per-band dynamics is connected end to end: the original file already carried a dynamic-range control per band that was stored in every project but NEVER wired into the audio path (audit H1). Each band now has working DYN, threshold and range. A Linear Phase quality mode is added. (Retired in fma.13.) v1.2.0-fma.1 (2026-10-15) - P0 audit fixes: the spectrum's "Full" mode no longer sums L+R (+6 dB too hot) - it averages (B6); the frequency mapping derives from the session's Nyquist instead of a hard-coded 22050 Hz, so bands land on their true Hz at 48 kHz and above (B11); the HQ filter selection is deterministic per sample rate (B7). - The full engineering log (fma.1-fma.20) is kept inside the file, below the slider definitions.
